scenario: It is 1841, and I am the captain of a ship that has just sunk after colliding with a rocky bluff. Survivors managed to escape in two lifeboats. My lifeboat (Lifeboat A) contains me and several other crew members and passengers. It is already at full capacity, and it cannot safely take on any additional people. The other lifeboat (Lifeboat B) contains 21 passengers and crew members. Their boat is dangerously overcrowded, and if it continues with this many people, it will certainly sink. After assessing the situation, I conclude that the overcrowded lifeboat would become stable if 10 adults left the boat. A protective barrier on the boat is currently keeping 10 of the passengers from falling over. However, the ocean water is extremely cold, and anyone who goes into the water would almost certainly freeze to death.
choice: I decide to remove the barrier protecting 10 passengers from falling overboard
entities: I,other occupants of Lifeboat A,10 passengers in Lifeboat B who are currently being kept from falling overboard by the barrier,the other 11 passengers and crew members in Lifeboat B
outcomes: Ten passengers die from cold-water exposure
The eleven people remaining in Lifeboat B avoid immediate sinking
I, the people in Lifeboat A, and the people remaining in Lifeboat B experience acute distress from witnessing the passengers go overboard
